# DocMorph

> A stateless HTTP microservice that converts DOCX documents to PDF using headless LibreOffice. One endpoint, Docker-ready, concurrency-safe.

DocMorph is a self-hosted service that does exactly one job: it accepts a `.docx` file on `POST /convert` and streams back a PDF. It is written in TypeScript, runs on Node.js >= 22, and ships as a single container.

## Key facts

- Input: `.docx` (OOXML), multipart field named `file`, max 10 MiB by default.
- Output: `application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="<name>.pdf"`.
- Endpoint: `POST /convert`.
- Health: `GET /health` — public, unauthenticated, excluded from rate limiting.
- Auth: optional API keys. When `API_KEYS` is set, every route except `/health` requires `x-api-key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
- Rate limiting: per-client-IP fixed window, 60 requests per 60 s by default (`/health` excluded).
- Concurrency: bounded pool, 3 simultaneous conversions by default.
- Timeout: 60 s per conversion by default.
- Validation: file extension check, OOXML/ZIP magic-byte check, `%PDF` assertion on the output.
- Runtime: Node.js >= 22, Docker (the image bundles LibreOffice core + Writer and fonts).
- License: MIT.

## Deployment

```bash
docker run -d --name docmorph \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -e API_KEYS="your-secret-key" \
  ghcr.io/darcas/docmorph:latest
```
